newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Straddles traded in British Telecom.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Straddles traded in British Telecom.

text.p: Traded options in British Telecommunications were busy on Monday with traders expecting the underlying shares to be volatile in coming months, dealers said.

By mid-afternoon, one of the largest deals was to buy 1,600 November 500 puts and calls at 34p and 25p each in BT in a long straddle strategy which will make a profit at expiry if the shares either go below 441p or above 559p.
In a separate deal, another trader bought 1,000 puts and calls in the same series and at the same prices.
By 1355 GMT, BT shares were down 12p to 489-1/2p.
Elsewhere, in British Steel the biggest deal was a crossed trade involving 500 July 160 puts traded at 23-1/2p as well as 500 October 160 puts that were also traded at 23-1/2p.

And in aero-engine manufacturer Rolls Royce, the main deal was from a seller of 400 November 220 puts at about 11p who must be prepared to buy the stock if the share price falls below 220p by expiry owing to assignment.
If the shares remain above 220p, the trader will collect 11p maximum profit.
Rolls Royce shares slipped 1/2p to 227-1/2p while those of British Steel were up 1/4p to 138p.

Over in index options, one large deal was a volatility trade in which a call spread was hedged by FTSE futures. It involved buying 750 September 4525 calls in European style FTSE at 319p and selling 750 September 4825 calls at 121p which was hedged by selling FTSE futures at 4800.
In general, increased implied market volatility should help the deal make money.
By 1355 GMT, cash FTSE was down 10.5 at 4802.3 while September futures were down three points at 4820.
